scenes.title: TITANIC
scenes.subtitle: The Last 2 Hours 40 Minutes
scenes.narration: April 14th, 1912. The biggest moving thing humans had ever built is racing across the North Atlantic. In less than three hours, it'll be gone.
Titanic was 269 metres long. People called her practically unsinkable, because her hull was split into sixteen watertight compartments.
She left Southampton on April 10th, picked up passengers in France and Ireland, and headed west for New York.

scenes.label: people on board
scenes.narration: About 2,224 people were on board. Millionaires in first class. Families in third class, chasing a new life.

scenes.title: Lifeboat seats vs people on board
scenes.narration: But here's the problem. Titanic had just twenty lifeboats, with room for 1,178 people. That's barely half.

scenes.title: Sunday, 14 April 1912
items: Several ice warnings received by radio
scenes.narration: On Sunday, the radio room got warning after warning about ice. The sea was flat calm, there was no moon, and the ship kept going at full speed.

scenes.label: ICEBERG RIGHT AHEAD
scenes.narration: 11:40 p.m. Lookout Frederick Fleet spots a dark shape dead ahead. He rings the bell three times. Iceberg, right ahead!
The officers swing the ship hard and throw the engines into reverse. Too late. The iceberg scrapes along the starboard side, below the waterline.
Five compartments start flooding. Titanic could survive four. With five, the water spills from one to the next, like an ice cube tray.

scenes.text: She is going to sink. An hour, perhaps an hour and a half.
scenes.by: Thomas Andrews, the ship's designer (as recalled by survivors)
scenes.narration: The ship's designer, Thomas Andrews, checks the damage and tells the captain the truth. She's going to sink. Fast.
Just after midnight, the crew uncovers the lifeboats. Distress calls go out. At about 12:45, the first boat is lowered into the dark.

scenes.label: people in Lifeboat 1
scenes.narration: But most passengers don't believe it. A small boat on a freezing sea feels more dangerous than the giant ship. So the first boats leave half empty. Lifeboat one? Just twelve people.
Help is coming. The Carpathia hears the call 58 miles away and races north through the ice. But she needs almost four hours.
By 2 a.m., the bow is underwater and the stern is lifting into the air. The last lifeboat leaves at 2:05.

scenes.label: TITANIC SINKS
scenes.narration: 2:20 a.m. Titanic breaks apart and sinks. Two hours and forty minutes after the collision.

scenes.title: In the water
items: Most people in the water died within minutes
scenes.narration: The water is minus two degrees. Hundreds of people are in it, and most die within minutes. Only one lifeboat goes back.

scenes.title: When Carpathia arrived
scenes.narration: Carpathia arrives around 4 a.m. She picks up about 700 survivors. More than 1,500 people are gone.

scenes.title: What changed after Titanic
items: Lifeboat seats for everyone on board
scenes.narration: Titanic changed the sea forever. Lifeboat seats for everyone. Radios on duty day and night. And an ice patrol that still watches the Atlantic today.

scenes.compare: About 4.5 times the height of the world's tallest building
scenes.narration: In 1985, explorers finally found the wreck. Almost four kilometres down, broken in two, just like some survivors said.

scenes.title: TITANIC
scenes.narration: She was built to be unsinkable. Instead, she taught the world that nothing is. Follow GetYr Studio for more stories like this.
